title: Meta and Carnegie Mellon study finds an RL-trained 8B model beats Llama-4-Maverick at tool selection
summary:
Smaller, cost-effective AI models outperforming larger ones could reshape AI development priorities, emphasizing efficiency over size.
The post Meta and Carnegie Mellon study finds an RL-trained 8B model beats Llama-4-Maverick at tool selection appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: A new study by Meta and Carnegie Mellon University reveals that a smaller, reinforcement learning-trained 8B AI model outperforms Llama-4-Maverick in tool selection tasks. This finding highlights a shift toward prioritizing model efficiency and cost-effectiveness over sheer size in artificial intelligence development, signaling potential changes in how future AI systems are built and deployed.

AI வளர்ச்சியில் அளவை விட செயல்திறனுக்கும் செலவுக் குறைப்புக்கும் முன்னுரிமை அளிக்கப்படுவதை இந்த முடிவு காட்டுகிறது.
